raw_findings.body: Dead field increases class surface without providing any diagnostic value; misleads maintainers into believing logging occurs in this class.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unused declaration silently persists as dead code, reducing maintainability and code review clarity.
raw_findings.impact: Dead field increases class surface without providing any diagnostic value; misleads maintainers into believing logging occurs in this class.
raw_findings.root_cause: A Logger field was copied from the parent class pattern but never wired into any log statement in the new class.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the unused logger field, or add meaningful logging calls (e.g. debug logs for permission evaluation) consistent with the parent ClientPermissions class.
raw_findings.title: Unused logger field added in ClientPermissionsV2
raw_findings.trigger: Any code path through ClientPermissionsV2 (e.g. calling canManage/canView/etc.)

raw_findings.body: Dead code remains in the class, retaining otherwise-unnecessary imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext) and misleading future maintainers into thinking client-based evaluation context is used for exchange-to logic in V2.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead code increases maintenance burden and creates a misleading impression that client-exchange evaluation is implemented in V2.
raw_findings.impact: Dead code remains in the class, retaining otherwise-unnecessary imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext) and misleading future maintainers into thinking client-based evaluation context is used for exchange-to logic in V2.
raw_findings.root_cause: Method was likely carried over from the V1 ClientPermissions implementation pattern during the creation of ClientPermissionsV2, but the corresponding caller (canExchangeTo) was replaced with an UnsupportedOperationException, leaving the helper orphaned.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the unused getEvaluationContext method (and now-unneeded imports) since canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission are unsupported in V2, or wire it into an actual evaluation path if V2 is expected to support it later.
raw_findings.title: Unused private helper method getEvaluationContext in ClientPermissionsV2
raw_findings.trigger: Compiling/reviewing ClientPermissionsV2; the method is never called because canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) now unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of using this context.

raw_findings.body: The retained `import java.util.Arrays;` becomes a dead/unused import, which under Keycloak's checkstyle UnusedImports rule will fail the build or generate a lint warning that must later be fixed in a follow-up commit.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Build/lint failure due to unused import detected by static analysis (checkstyle).
raw_findings.impact: The retained `import java.util.Arrays;` becomes a dead/unused import, which under Keycloak's checkstyle UnusedImports rule will fail the build or generate a lint warning that must later be fixed in a follow-up commit.
raw_findings.root_cause: Deleting the only call site of Arrays.asList without auditing remaining imports for the file.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the now-unused `import java.util.Arrays;` statement from UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java alongside the other cleaned-up imports (equalTo, Collectors, AbstractPolicyRepresentation).
raw_findings.title: Removed method left `java.util.Arrays` import unused
raw_findings.trigger: Compile/build the module after this patch removes the private createUserPermission(Logic, UserRepresentation, Set, UserPolicyRepresentation...) helper, which was the only remaining use of java.util.Arrays in the file (the import itself was left in place).

raw_findings.body: Adds pointless object construction and obscures intent, making the test harder to read and increasing the chance a future edit misuses UserConfigBuilder here believing it has semantic effect (e.g. assuming it also updates the user).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reduced code readability/maintainability; no functional break but a code-review-worthy smell introduced by the patch.
raw_findings.impact: Adds pointless object construction and obscures intent, making the test harder to read and increasing the chance a future edit misuses UserConfigBuilder here believing it has semantic effect (e.g. assuming it also updates the user).
raw_findings.root_cause: Refactor mechanically rewrapped the previous UserRepresentation-based call, but did not simplify the redundant builder usage to the already-available id string.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass newUserId directly: createPermission(client, newUserId, usersType, Set.of(MANAGE), policy);
raw_findings.title: Unnecessary UserConfigBuilder round-trip to obtain an already-known user id
raw_findings.trigger: Reading/maintaining this test after the refactor: newUserId is already a String obtained a few lines above, but the call builds a throwaway UserConfigBuilder/UserRepresentation solely to re-extract the same id via .build().getId().

raw_findings.failure_mode: Style/formatting inconsistency flagged by linters or future diffs, no functional impact.
raw_findings.impact: Inconsistent code style within the same file/method group, which will likely trigger formatter/checkstyle diffs on next touch and reduces readability consistency introduced by this patch.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Run the project formatter or manually add the missing space after the comma in all affected createUserPolicy(realm, client, ...) call sites in this file.
